note:
ISO 2026-W17 runs from April 20 through April 26. Mars and Saturn are separated by about 0.0° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mercury and Mars are separated by about 0.7° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌓 First Quarter — 02:31:46 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Merak, Dubhe as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -7.3; direct motion; 9.2% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Jupiter in ecliptic longitude Apr 22 22:51 UTC. Mercury: Naked eye; magnitude -0.1; direct motion; 71.7% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mars in ecliptic longitude Apr 20 21:44 UTC. Conjunction with Saturn in ecliptic longitude Apr 20 11:22 UTC. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 90.4% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Uranus in ecliptic longitude Apr 24 01:58 UTC. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 1.2; direct motion; 98.1% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Apr 20 21:44 UTC. Ceres: In solar glare; magnitude 8.9; direct motion; 99.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.1; direct motion; 99.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Apr 22 22:51 UTC. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.9; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Apr 20 11:22 UTC. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Venus in ecliptic longitude Apr 24 01:58 UTC. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace the charted figure of Crt, then identify Alkes at its plotted position. Trace the charted figure of Crt, then identify β Crt at its plotted position.

story_candidates.dek: Arp 206 is an observing target in LMi carried by the weekly Calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected Arp 206 as one of this week’s fixed-sky observing targets.

How to find it: Establish the preserved LMi constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

story_candidates.dek: Alkes is a star in Crt of catalogue visual magnitude 4.08; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
The stored catalogue gives a visual magnitude of 4.08. This is a catalogue value, not a prediction of its brightness this week. Lower magnitudes mean brighter objects; sky brightness and altitude affect whether you can see the star.

Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 10h 59m and declination -18.3°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star rises and sets, reaching approximately 27° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Crt constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
